texts.preamble: M/S Dwarka Trading Company vs State Th. Capd Deptt on 1 October, 2021 Author: Rajnesh Oswal Bench: Rajnesh Oswal Sr. No. 29 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh At Jammu Owp No. 295/2010 (O&M) M/s Dwarka Trading Company .....Appellant(s)/Petitioner(s) Through: Mr. Supreet Singh Johal, Adv. Vs State Th. Capd Deptt. ..... Respondent(s) Through: Mr. H. A. Siddiqui, Sr. Aag Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rajnesh Oswal, Judge Order 1. The present writ petition has been filed by the petitioner for declaring the SRO No. 180 dated 4th of June, 2003 and SRO No.407 dated 4th of December, 2003 as ultra-vires to the Articles 14, 19 and 301 of the Constitution of India as they were beyond the scope of the provisions of Section 3 of the Essential Commodities (EC) Act.
texts.facts: Order 1. The present writ petition has been filed by the petitioner for declaring the SRO No. 180 dated 4th of June, 2003 and SRO No.407 dated 4th of December, 2003 as ultra-vires to the Articles 14, 19 and 301 of the Constitution of India as they were beyond the scope of the provisions of Section 3 of the Essential Commodities (EC) Act. 2. Reply has been filed by the respondents in which it is stated that matter was taken up with the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Department of Consumer Affairs, Govt of India and as per the minutes of the meetings, it was decided that the State Government would re-consider the matter keeping in view the fact that the Prevention Of Food Adulteration (PFA), Act had necessary provision for which the State Government was considering the issue of proposed order. It was also decided that in case the State Government still felt that a separate order has to be issued under EC Act, they would provide detailed justification for issue of such an order under the EC Act when similar provisions were made available in the PFA Act. Thereafter respondents No. 6 and 7 took up the matter with the Health and Medical Education Department of then State and the said department made the following observations: "that the Govt of Indian Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has already issued M/S Dwarka Trading Company vs State Th. Capd Deptt on 1 October, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55186490/ 1 Notification vide GSR No. 670(E) dated 17- 11-2005 under PFA rules, 1955, as such, there is no need to issue any separate order under the PFA Act, 1955 and the rules made thereunder as the said Notification is also applicable to J&K State". 3.
